plain: To rob by force, especially in war

webster.text: To pillage; to spoil; to strip; to take the goods of an enemy by open force.

example.quote: From a deficiency in this particular, one of two evils must ensue; either the people must be subjected to continual plunder, as a substitute for a more eligible mode of supplying the public wants, or the government must sink into a fatal atrophy, and, in a short course of time, perish.
